problem: final_mission_r12 and r13 (world 'shipped', 20 km/h search) stalled STUCK at x=9.94 at the mouth of the return slalom's second slot (1.0 m wide against the simulation's 2 x 0.45 m). r10 had passed the same slot 3 cm off centre with 0.466/0.471 m; corridor code and world were byte-identical between r10 and r12.
root_cause: The planner preferred the straight line at the bare 0.45 m clearance (and fell to the zero-reserve tier when no lattice row fitted the 5 cm reserve band) over a route keeping the 2.5 cm sampling reserve; on recorded scans it routed 0.450-0.457 m from the block corner.
Once 1-2 cm inside the clearance, every command (the planned recentre sidestep included) was certified against 0.45 m from its start point, which it already failed.

The nose lidar (0.139 m ahead of base_link) with the masked 150-210 deg rear sector never observes the strip beside the body centre; only a 2.5 cm-wide body-to-sensor link counted as observed, so every sideways step over 2.5 cm was refused. The kinematic test harness put the lidar at the body origin and could not reproduce this.
